newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Investors pour $11 billion into Swiss mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Investors pour $11 billion into Swiss mutual funds.

text.p: Switzerland's mountain of cash continues to rise, with mostly foreign investors pouring about $11.2 billion into Swiss mutual funds in the 12 months to end of March, a new market survey said on Wednesday.

Statistician Bopp ISB said combined assets of public mutual funds set up by Swiss banks at home and abroad grew 16.3 billion Swiss francs to 249 billion francs ($170 billion) at end-March compared with a year ago.
Bankers say the Swiss mutual fund industry is expanding fast with many banks seeking innovative niches in a market where assets grew by 26 percent in 1996.
Bopp ISB said the volume of mutual fund assets grew by 6.9 billion Swiss francs in the first three months of the year and 1.8 billion in the month of March but gave no year-ago comparisons.
In January, the volume of mutual fund assets jumped by a whopping 9.9 billion Swiss francs, which bankers say was mainly because of seasonally high liquidity at the start of the year.
Bopp ISB gave no breakdown for contributions to asset growth from net cash flows and from market performance.
Secretive Swiss banks do not publish data on the volume of client assets in Switzerland, where total private wealth under management is estimated at more than $1.8 trillion.
Bankers estimate that the volume of net cash flows into Switzerland's banks and asset management institutions grew by some 10 percent in the first quarter of the year.

Nicholas Fliess, of Intrag fund managing firm for Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), said investors were taking cash out of bond funds because of lower Swiss interest rates and market uncertainty, but flows to asset allocation funds were rising.
The market leader is Swiss Bank Corporation with a 30 percent share, followed by UBS with 26 percent.

The Bopp ISB survey covers only public funds and not inhouse funds managed by private banks which do not publish data. It also excludes foreign groups selling mutual funds in Switzerland such as Fidelity, Flemings, Citibank and Nomura.

Bankers say foreigners make up the bulk of their mutual fund clients. A recent survey by Swiss asset management firm Swissca said only one out of 10 Swiss investors had cash in mutual funds. Two-thirds of Swiss-managed mutual funds are based in Luxembourg.
--- Elif Kaban, Geneva Newsroom 41-22-733 38 31 ($ = 1.462 Swiss Francs)
